pick.name: Next.js 16 (App Router) + shadcn/ui
pick.what: React meta-framework for SaaS, marketing and API routes
pick.why: Largest ecosystem (61.8M weekly downloads), deepest Claude Code familiarity, every auth/AI/payments SDK documents it first; Adapter API stable since 16.2 so not tied to Vercel
pick.free_limits: Framework free. NOTE Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only - commercial SaaS needs Vercel Pro or another host

alts.name: TanStack Start
alts.what: Type-safe full-stack React on Vite (server functions, SPA mode)
alts.why: Simpler than RSC, deploys anywhere incl. Cloudflare; same Vite build reusable as Electron renderer
alts.maintained: @tanstack/react-start 1.169.4 (2026-10-22); 1.0 stable announced 2026-10-13 (RC was 2025-09-23); security advisory CVE-2026-102989 on 2026-09-30

alts.name: React Router 8 (framework mode)
alts.what: Remix successor; SSR or SPA on Vite
alts.why: Mature, adapter-based, easy SPA for desktop

candidates.name: Next.js (pick)
candidates.verdict: Default for SaaS + SEO pages; complexity of RSC/caching is the cost.

candidates.name: TanStack Start
candidates.verdict: Wins for dashboard-style apps, Cloudflare hosting, or when the same Vite app must ship inside Electron. 1.0 is only ~2 weeks old - revisit in 2027.

candidates.name: React Router 8
candidates.verdict: Solid, smaller ecosystem than Next; good SPA story.

candidates.name: SvelteKit 3.1
candidates.verdict: Excellent DX/perf but no code sharing with React Native.

candidates.name: Astro 7.4
candidates.verdict: Best for marketing/docs sites; use alongside, not as the app framework.

candidates.name: Vite + React SPA
candidates.verdict: Fine for desktop renderer; no SSR for marketing/SEO.

decision: Next.js stays the pick on ecosystem and agent familiarity, now with a stable adapter API so hosting is not locked to Vercel. Switch to TanStack Start for app-only products deployed on Cloudflare or bundled into the desktop app.
note: Consolidated: deploy Next.js to Cloudflare Workers with the OpenNext adapter (@opennextjs/cloudflare, needs Next.js 16.2.3 or later), matching the default deploy stack. If the adapter blocks a feature, build that app with TanStack Start or React Router instead. Vercel only on Pro ($20/mo), because Hobby is non-commercial.
details: Vercel Hobby: 'restricted to non-commercial personal use only' (fair-use page, updated 2026-09-14). Hosting choice is another track's slot.

verify.note: Next.js pick sound; Vercel Hobby non-commercial caveat correctly included.
